name: Bitcoin
day_summary: BTC closed the June 19 UTC day at $63,544.43 — $44 above the $63,500 two-day stop threshold. The Day 2 stop clock DID NOT EXECUTE. Stop clock RESETS. The June 19 UTC session was brutal through mid-day: BTC fell to $62,313.01 at 09:00 UTC (the session's deepest point) on thin Juneteenth holiday liquidity with US ETF desks dark. The recovery began at the 13:00 UTC candle and extended through the afternoon before the decisive final rally: the 23:00 UTC candle (open $63,325, high $63,671, close $63,544) closed the day above the stop level. The two-consecutive-UTC-close condition for stop execution was NOT met: Day 1 confirmed $62,952.75 (June 18 UTC close), Day 2 CLEARED $63,544.43 (June 19 UTC close — above $63,500). Macro context at UTC midnight: DXY at ~100.79 (settled from an intraday one-year high of 101.13 on Juneteenth FX); VIX confirmed at 16.40 on June 18 (below the <17 gate — gate CLEARED; corrects the earlier 17.0 reading); Hormuz commercial traffic beginning to flow after the US-Iran MOU; Switzerland talks postponed but not canceled (JD Vance logistics, Israel-Hezbollah complication). Live price at 01:03 UTC June 20: $63,508 — hovering $8 above the stop level. The stop survives; the thesis is on life support.
long_pnl: longs from the June 15 re-entry at $65–$66K are approximately 4% offside at $63,544; the stop framework DID NOT execute — position is held; the $62,313 intraday low represented the worst point of the session but was not close-confirmed; the late recovery above $63,500 on thin Juneteenth tape extends the framework to June 20 UTC midnight
short_pnl: bears were winning all day until the final two hours: BTC traded below $63,500 for most of June 19 UTC (approximately 20 of 24 hours), but the daily close framework requires a close, not intraday sustain; the $63,544 UTC close thwarted stop execution by $44; IBIT outflow streak continues, Fear & Greed at 15, DXY at 100.79 — short fundamentals intact but the technical stop trigger was avoided

decision.rationale: HOLD — STOP CLOCK RESET. BTC closed the June 19 UTC day at $63,544.43, $44 above the $63,500 stop threshold. The next key date is June 20 UTC midnight close — a fresh Day 1 trigger requires BTC to close below $63,500 again. For the position to survive, BTC needs to close above $63,500 on June 20 UTC. Current live price at 01:03 UTC June 20 is $63,508 — the situation remains precarious. Do NOT add to the position. Underlying bearish factors are unchanged: DXY 100.79, IBIT 11-day outflow streak, Fear & Greed at 15. The stop surviving by $44 is a technical reprieve, not a fundamental reversal. Maintain the framework: new stop trigger if BTC closes below $63,500 on any June 20+ UTC session; two consecutive closes below = exit full position. Alternative immediate exit signal: intraday conviction break below $62,313 (today's session low) without recovery — do not wait for the two-day clock in that scenario.
